title: Local MAP Sampling for Diffusion Models
creator: Shaorong Zhang, Rob Brekelmans, Greg Ver Steeg
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shaorong Zhang, Rob Brekelmans, Greg Ver Steeg. Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS) provides a principled Bayesian approach to inverse problems by sampling from p ⁡ ( x 0 ∣ y ) p(x_{0}\mid y) . However, in practice, the goal of inverse problem solving is not to cover the posterior but to recover the most accurate reconstruction, where optimization-based diffusion solvers often excel despite lacking a clear probabilistic foundation.

title: Enhancing Maritime Object Detection in Real-Time with RT-DETR and Data Augmentation
creator: Nader Nemati
description: Abstract Maritime object detection faces essential challenges due to the small target size and limitations of labeled real RGB data. This paper will present a real-time object detection system based on RT-DETR, enhanced by employing augmented synthetic images while strictly evaluating on real data.

title: SpotDiff: Spotting and Disentangling Interference in Feature Space for Subject-Preserving Image Generation
creator: Yongzhi Li, Saining Zhang, Yibing Chen, Boying Li, Yanxin Zhang, Xiaoyu Du
description: Abstract Personalized image generation aims to faithfully preserve a reference subject’s identity while adapting to diverse text prompts. Existing optimization-based methods ensure high fidelity but are computationally expensive, while learning-based approaches offer efficiency at the cost of entangled representations influenced by nuisance factors. We introduce SpotDiff, a novel learning-based method that extracts subject-specific features by spotting and disentangling interference.

title: Bioinspired Tapered-Spring Turbulence Sensor for Underwater Flow Detection
creator: Xiao Jin, Zhenhua Yu*, Thrishantha Nanayakkara
description: Abstract This paper presents a bio-inspired underwater whisker sensor for robust hydrodynamic disturbance detection and efficient signal analysis based on Physical Reservoir Computing (PRC). The design uses a tapered nylon spring with embedded accelerometers to achieve spatially distributed vibration sensing and frequency separation along the whisker.

title: Quantum Algorithm for Binary Vector Encoding and Retrieval Utilizing the Permutation Trick
creator: Andreas Wichert
description: Abstract We present a novel quantum storage algorithm for k k binary vectors of dimension m m into a superposition of a m m -qubit quantum state based on a permutation technique. We compare this algorithm to the storage algorithm proposed by Ventura and Martinez.

title: A Zone-Based Algorithm for Timed Parity Games
creator: Gilles Geeraerts, Frédéric Herbreteau, Jean-François Raskin, Alexis Reynouard
description: Abstract This paper revisits timed games by building upon the semantics introduced in “The Element of Surprise in Timed Games” [ 9 ] . We introduce some modifications to this semantics for two primary reasons: firstly, we recognize instances where the original semantics appears counterintuitive in the context of controller synthesis; secondly, we present methods to develop efficient zone-based algorithms.

title: Base Models Know How to Reason, Thinking Models Learn When
creator: Constantin VenhoffUniversity of OxfordUnited Kingdom constantin@robots.ox.ac.uk, Iván ArcuschinUniversity of Buenos AiresArgentina iarcuschin@dc.uba.ar Philip TorrUniversity of OxfordUnited KingdomArthur ConmyNeel Nanda
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Constantin VenhoffUniversity of OxfordUnited Kingdom constantin@robots.ox.ac.uk, Iván ArcuschinUniversity of Buenos AiresArgentina iarcuschin@dc.uba.ar Philip TorrUniversity of OxfordUnited KingdomArthur ConmyNeel Nanda. Why do thinking language models like DeepSeek R1 outperform their base counterparts? Despite consistent performance gains, it remains unclear to what extent thinking models learn entirely new reasoning capabilities or repurpose pre-existing base model ones.

title: Axion Quality Problem: Keep Calm and Baryon
creator: Prateek Agrawal, Anson Hook, Vazha Loladze, and Mario Reig
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Prateek Agrawal, Anson Hook, Vazha Loladze, and Mario Reig. Axion models generically suffer from a severe quality problem when coupled to gravity. In this article we provide a very simple model with a high quality axion. The axion is a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of the baryon number symmetry, U ​ ( 1 ) B U(1)_{B} , of a new composite sector that breaks U ​ ( 1 ) B U(1)_{B} spontaneously when it confines.

title: RIGEL: Feedback-regulated cloud-scale star formation efficiency in a simulated dwarf galaxy merger
creator: Yunwei Deng, Hui Li, Federico Marinacci, Yang Ni, Boyuan Liu, Aaron Smith, Rahul Kannan, Greg L. Bryan
description: Abstract Major mergers of galaxies are likely to trigger bursty star formation activities. Usually, the accumulation of dense gas and the boost of star formation efficiency (SFE) are considered to be the two main drivers of starbursts. However, it remains unclear how each process operates on the scale of individual star-forming clouds.

title: geko : A tool for modelling galaxy kinematics and morphology in JWST /NIRCam slitless spectroscopic observations 2025 geko : A tool for modelling galaxy kinematics and morphology in JWST /NIRCam slitless spectroscopic observations – 16
creator: A. Lola Danhaive, Sandro Tacchella
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. Lola Danhaive, Sandro Tacchella. Wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) is a powerful tool for studying large samples of galaxies across cosmic times. With the arrival of JWST , and its NIRCAM grism mode, slitless spectroscopy can reach a medium spectral resolution of ( R ∼ 1600 ) (R\sim 1600) , allowing it to spatially resolve the ionised-gas kinematics out to z ∼ 9 z\sim 9 .

creator: T. Zhang, E. Charles, J.F. Crenshaw, S.J. Schmidt, P. Adari, J. Gschwend, S. Mau, B. Andrews, E. Aubourg, Y. Bains, K. Bechtol, A. Boucaud, D. Boutigny, P. Burchat, J. Chevalier, J.
